<description>
Fixes #36483

As described in the linked issue, migration to descriptor wallets currently fails for legacy wallets that contain no spendable keys and are tracking watch-only transactions.

When a database transaction containing `RemoveTxs()` is aborted, the database rolls back and the registered `on_abort` callback is invoked. The current listener contains an empty `std::function` so calling it throws `std::bad_function_call` and masks the actual migration error.

The first commit changes the callback to a no-op function since no memory cleanup happens on abort. It also adds a unit test to confirm that abort restores the database record and leaves wallet memory unchanged.

After this commit, the [functional test](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36483) supplied by the issue's author reports `Error: Not all transaction records were migrated (-4)`, exposing the migration error previously masked by the abort callback exception.

During wallet migration, `RemoveTxs()` defers deletion of transactions from the original wallet's in-memory `mapWallet` until after the database commit. The current check that requires an empty map before the database commit causes migration  to fail.

The second commit checks that the transaction IDs left in the map exactly match those already scheduled to be removed in the `txids_to_delete` vector. If they match, migration continues and the `on_commit` callback removes those transactions from memory.

A new functional test is added to cover migration of a blank wallet with watch-only transactions. It checks that the destination watch-only wallet retains both transactions and balance, including after unloading and reloading the wallet, without rescanning the blockchain.
</description>

<commits>
e518ef26f4 fix(wallet): Handle abort of transaction removal

Aborting a RemoveTxs() transaction invokes an empty std::function, which
throws `std::bad_function_call`.

Implement a no-op abort callback since memory changes are deferred until
after database commit. Extend RemoveTxs coverage to verify rollback
restores the database record and leaves wallet memory unchanged.

6ed50582c1 fix(wallet): Fix watch-only migration failure

Removing transactions updates `mapWallet` only after database commit.
Requiring an empty map beforehand causes migration of legacy wallets
containing only watch-only transactions to fail.

Require all transactions in map to be those already scheduled for
removal. Add regression coverage to ensure transactions and balances are
preserved after migration and wallet reload without having to rescan
blockchain

Co-authored-by: David Gumberg <davidzgumberg@gmail.com>
</commits>
